author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The fix makes `/owners?page=0` and negative page values render the first page instead of the error page — a normalized-input behavior of the same kind already recorded for REQ-OWN-002 (edge case 1: a search that is entirely spaces normalizes to an empty search). REQ-OWN-002's 'Done when' bullets and edge-case list are silent on out-of-range page numbers, so a reader of the PRD alone cannot tell this clamping is an intended, tested product behavior rather than an implementation accident. Recommend a new numbered edge case under REQ-OWN-002 stating that a page below the first is shown as the first page rather than an error, in behavioral language with no reference to the request parameter or the clamp mechanism.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Upper bound remains unvalidated: `page` is clamped only from below. A very large value (roughly above 429,496,729, where pageNumber * pageSize exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE) makes the resulting offset unrepresentable for the JPA first-result, which is expected to surface as a 500 error page rather than the graceful first-page/not-found response. I could not execute the app to confirm the exact threshold, so this is reported as unverified reachability, not a defect: the demonstrated harm is a generic error page (server.error.include-message/include-stacktrace stay at Boot defaults, so no internals leak) and no unbounded allocation or expensive query occurs. Worth a follow-up requirement to clamp the top end (for example to paginated.getTotalPages()) so the whole `page` domain has one defined behavior.

Non-numeric or out-of-int-range values (`/owners?page=abc`, `/owners?page=99999999999`) still fail binding with a 400 rather than rendering the first page, so the endpoint now answers three different ways for three flavours of the same malformed input. No security impact, but the inconsistency is worth a product decision alongside the upper-bound clamp.

VetController.showVetList still binds `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page` with no clamp (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetController.java:45), so /vets.html?page=0 keeps the pre-existing behaviour this slice fixed for owners. Out of REQ-OWN-002 scope and unchanged by this diff, but it is the same class and leaves the codebase with two different treatments of the same concern.

No NVD matching ran in this review: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle (plugins are spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47, nohttp 0.0.11) and this reviewer has no network access. The slice adds no dependencies, so the posture is unchanged, but the framework versions remain not verified against the NVD by this pass — a human or CI should close that check. The existing cyclonedx SBOM task is the natural hook.

Pre-existing and out of scope: application.properties sets management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=* with its own "don't do this in production" comment. Untouched by this change, noted so it is not mistaken for a clean read of the deployment config.
approved_aspects: Clamp is applied before every downstream use: `int page = Math.max(requestedPage, FIRST_PAGE)` sits at the top of processFindForm, so findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (PageRequest.of(page - 1, 5)) and addPaginationModel (model attribute `currentPage`) both receive the clamped value; the raw `requestedPage` is not referenced again.
No integer underflow: page >= 1 after the clamp makes `page - 1` >= 0, so PageRequest.of can no longer receive a negative index. Integer.MIN_VALUE as input clamps to 1 rather than wrapping.

Untrusted input reaches no sensitive sink: `page` is an int used only as a page index, never interpolated into a query, path, shell command, or log message. Repository access stays on the derived-query method findByLastNameStartingWith (no string-built JPQL).

Output escaping unchanged and safe: `currentPage` is an int rendered through Thymeleaf th:text in owners/ownersList.html; no user-derived string is added to the model by this change and no template-preprocessing (__${...}__) is introduced.
Mass-assignment guard intact: the @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") still applies to the `Owner` command object on this endpoint, and the bound Owner is read-only here (only getLastName).
No new error-path information disclosure: the change removes an error-page path rather than adding one; no exception messages, stack traces, or internal details are surfaced.
No dependency, configuration, or build change in the diff, so the supply-chain surface is unchanged by this slice.

Test exercises the boundary from the outside through MockMvc (real binding and dispatch) at both 0 and -1, and asserts the clamped Pageable reaching the repository (getPageNumber() == 0), which is the security-relevant assertion.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: A page request before the first shows the first page of owner matches
summary: Asking for a page of owner search matches earlier than the first shows the first page instead of an error page, matching the normalized-input behavior already recorded for whitespace-only searches.
acceptance_criteria: given a search whose results are paged, when a page before the first is asked for, then the first page of matches is shown
given a page before the first, when the results are shown, then no error page is presented
non_goals: a page request beyond the last page
notes: Round 2 findings processing: doc-reviewer clarify finding on docs/prd.md#req-own-002. Recorded the behavior as edge case 4 under Owner records, in behavioral language beside edge case 1 (whitespace-only search normalizes to an empty search). Edge cases 1-3 keep their numbers. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. No prd-autofix records since the last prd-entry, so the autofix audit found nothing to judge.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Retrospective triage of a landed fix. The clamp is request-binding normalization at the web trust boundary, not a domain rule, so it sits exactly where architecture-principles.md places it: the Web controller row admits binding and response selection, and security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries requires range validation before use at the point external input arrives. It therefore does not count as a fresh business rule in a controller under the deviation clause of architecture-principles.md line 91, and system-design.md § Package Structure and the OwnerController contract row need no change. One small addition made: a Threat Model row recording the paging-parameter surface, since this slice closes one instance of it and leaves others open.
integration_points: docs/system-design.md § Threat Model gains one row: internal exception text disclosed through a rejected paging parameter, mitigated partially by the owner-search clamp
no change to § Contracts, § Constants, § Package Structure, or § Known Defects

patterns.description: Normalize an out-of-contract request parameter once, at the binding site, before it reaches any collaborator. The clamped value flows to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so the Pageable handed to the repository and the currentPage shown in the model cannot disagree. This is the shape any later paging clamp should copy, including the veterinarian list.

FIRST_PAGE stays a private constant and is deliberately absent from § Constants, which lists only constants whose value is load-bearing across files. It is the same class of private routing detail as the view-name constants that section already excludes.

risks.risk: VetController.showVetList carries the identical unclamped shape, so /vets.html?page=0 still renders the error page. The two paging surfaces now diverge, and the divergence is invisible from either file alone.
risks.mitigation: Recorded in the new § Threat Model row rather than in § Known Defects. Calling it a defect is a product judgment with no owner decision behind it, and the PRD holds veterinarian paging as an explicit non-goal for this slice.

risks.risk: A non-numeric or out-of-int-range page value fails request binding and reaches the error page, which renders the exception message per the confirmed Known Defect breaching REQ-SYS-002. The clamp does not cover this path.
risks.mitigation: Named in the same Threat Model row. The durable fix is the error page itself, not another controller clamp; that work belongs to REQ-SYS-002.

notes: Verdict rationale. Not covered: the slice leaves a security-relevant state change that no existing section records. Not new: no new pattern, type, package, dependency, or boundary was introduced. Not conflicting: the fix aligns REQ-OWN-002 behavior with the normalized-input treatment already recorded for whitespace-only search. No ADR written: the clamp is a single reversible expression with no rejected alternative carrying a real trade-off, which fails the adr-template threshold. The three non-goals (page beyond the last, non-numeric or out-of-range values, veterinarian paging) are product decisions awaiting an owner; a non-goal ADR for them is the product-requirements-expert's channel, not mine. Accuracy note for whoever picks up the beyond-last non-goal: it is not an exception path. PageRequest.of accepts the index, the repository returns an empty page, and processFindForm takes the isEmpty branch, so the reader sees the search form reporting no owner found rather than the error page. The Threat Model row was written to exclude that case deliberately. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit found nothing to judge. Coverage claim basis: grep over the owner and vet packages plus a full read of both controllers; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, which is the weaker basis.
